pest_name: Sweet Potato Leaf Feathery Mottle Virus
history: SPLFMV is closely related to SPFMV and has been identified worldwide, commonly as part of sweet potato viral disease (SPVD).

proteins.name: HC-Pro
proteins.function: Proteinase, aids in aphid transmission, long-distance movement

proteins.name: CI
proteins.function: Cytoplasmic inclusion protein, RNA helicase activity

proteins.name: Cistron
proteins.function: Coat protein, virion assembly, viral transmission, spread

life_cycle.entry: Mechanical transmission or via aphid stylets piercing leaf tissue
life_cycle.replication: Genome translated into polyprotein, cleaved by P1, HC-Pro, NIa proteases
life_cycle.gene_silencing_suppression: HC-Pro suppresses siRNA and miRNA in leaf cells

transmission.mechanism: Non-persistent via stylet tips during leaf feeding

symptoms.typical: Feathery or mottled patterns on leaves, light to dark purple or green

co-infections.SPVD: When co-infected with SPCSV, causes stunting, mosaic leaves, reduced yield

strains.name: C
strains.location: Australia, Africa, Asia, North and South America

agricultural_impact.yield_loss: Significant when combined in SPVD; reduces photosynthetic efficiency and plant vigor
agricultural_impact.social_impact: Affects smallholder farmers relying on sweet potato leaves as food and fodder

management.early_detection: Monitor leaf symptoms and confirm via ELISA
management.removal: Rogue infected plants to prevent spread

references: Based on SPFMV research and sweet potato viral disease studies
